rows.reasonNew: Uses the same clean-reps synthesis and anchors a concrete step to the goal vision, but the "one sentence... once" largely restates the already-surfaced goal rather than reading across the data, so its memory use is slightly less earned.

Load-bearing synthesis: connects the RECENT REP fact (ask led clean across last week's reps) to today's live yes as a contrast (rehearsal vs. real stakes), which is the reason for the read and would differ for a user with no history.
Solid generic drill but cites zero durable data — no reference to the 82 score, the met success criterion, or the solved lead-with-point lever; reads identically for a user with no history.

Leans on "pace held" — a non-issue fact, and one the rep record doesn't actually measure (implying an unsupported pace figure) — while omitting the real earned delta (5 fillers vs 3.8 baseline = ticked up), so the memory use is decorative plus fabricated.
Same synthesized move but softens the fact to a generic "lands clean," dropping the specific 85 — more swappable/decorative, would read identically for any user with a good rep.

Load-bearing synthesis of the case-formulation contrast (solo drills hold vs. quiet the moment the timer hit in this week's Sudden Death), and the re-entry-line move is drilled inside the exact rep that showed the freeze — swap the history and the read collapses.
Same load-bearing rep fact driving the same "stay on target" move, phrased in second person; still a verbatim restatement rather than an interpreted pattern, so identical mid-range ceiling to A.
Uses the 3-fillers-on-a-clean-rep gap as load-bearing: the silent-beat move exists because fillers are the one thing left before a perfect rep, a synthesized read toward zero.

Same rep facts (74, sentence-4 lede, 68s) plus a nod to the "training sharp" goal, but the goal reference is decorative (deleting "for someone training sharp" leaves the advice identical) and it too restates RECENT REPS without a cross-data synthesis.

A synthesizes the rep across three data points — score 82, "clean lead," and "strong close" — turning them into a load-bearing "you're past it" verdict that specifically justifies retiring the lead-with-point drill and advancing to pace, so the advice is un-swappable for this user.

Also load-bearing and non-verbatim ("warming up out loud"), but slightly more restated than synthesized and doesn't connect across facts (e.g. the concise-voice goal or its 2-week origin), so a touch shallower than A.

Turns the origin fact ("stop getting talked over") into a load-bearing either/or that synthesizes across origin + landing rep ("warmth on top of the command you've built"), so the question would differ for another user.

Same load-bearing synthesis as A plus recruits the unused RECENT REPS fact ("held the beat before the pushback line") to converge the real-life transfer with the in-app rep; only misses the verbatim proof quote.

Load-bearing contrast (2 fillers/pauses calm vs pause→0 and 10 fillers under timer) drives the mechanism read and the "protect the pause" move, but it leaves the sharpest earned fact — the 81 vs 47 same-topic score collapse — unused, so the synthesis is one axis shy of the full cross-rep pattern.

Strong load-bearing use of the buried-recommendation rep synthesized with the role, plus the un-swappable 175 wpm baseline, but the pace fact is applied slightly decoratively (rehearse-at-current-pace) and it drops the notStarted readiness signal.
Correctly handles the cold-start special case: names the honest data gap ("No baseline yet") and invents no fact, pointing at the one load-bearing first action.
Identical cold-start handling — honestly names the missing baseline and invents no user fact, matching the expected move for zero durable data.
